144: (3) Just as it is forbidden to cook with fire, so too it is forbidden to cook with toldos ha'or (derivatives of fire). For example: placing an egg beside a pot, or breaking it on a cloth that was heated by fire, in order to roast it. And even with toldos chamah (derivatives of the sun), such as a cloth heated in the sun — it is forbidden as a decree lest it be confused with toldos ha'or. And likewise it is forbidden to bury it in sand or road dust that was heated by the power of the sun. But in the sun itself — for example placing an egg in the sun, or placing water in the sun to be warmed — it is permitted.
147: (9) 'That it is forbidden to cook' — one who cooks with toldos ha'or is liable.
149: (11) 'Or to break it, etc., and even, etc., but' — three distinctions regarding the egg in Beitza 2b, see Rashi there.
151: (3) 'To insulate it' — see the Beer Heitev. See also Noda B'Yehuda second edition, chapter 23, who writes that the rule that salted is like heated applies specifically to roasting, and is a Torah-level matter regarding absorption like a vessel; but it cannot be considered like roasting to render it forbidden as bishul on Shabbos or to forbid Pesach meat that was salted on account of roasting — see there.
153: (17) 'With toldos ha'or' — one who cooks with them is liable. Therefore, one who places fruits or water on the oven or inside the heating stove after the oven has been fired up, and they cooked there, is liable. And by rabbinic law it is forbidden to place them even before the oven is fired up, as explained later. And all the laws of cooking mentioned in this siman apply also to something cooked by means of toldos ha'or.
155: (18) 'And even with derivatives of the sun' — even b'dieved it is forbidden, and it is possible that after Shabbos it is permitted even to the one who cooked [Chiddushei R' Akiva Eiger].
157: (19) 'To insulate it, etc.' — this applies even before Shabbos, because sand is something that adds heat, as explained above in siman 257 seif 3, and it is forbidden to insulate with it even before Shabbos as explained there.
159: (20) 'In sand' — even if one does not insulate it but merely rolls it on Shabbos on hot sand so that it will roast, it is also forbidden as a decree on account of toldos ha'or. Therefore it is forbidden to roast an egg on Shabbos in sand heated by the sun.
161: (21) 'But in the sun itself' — the Sages did not decree on account of fire, for the sun and fire are not confused with each other.
164: 'And even in derivatives of the sun, etc.' — see the Mishna Berurah that leaving food in derivatives of the sun is permitted, and in Chiddushei R' Akiva Eiger he inclines to say that even in toldos ha'or it is permitted to leave food, for it is no worse than a swept-out stove — see there. And to insulate in sand heated by the sun is forbidden according to all.
166: 'To insulate it in sand' — see the Peri Megadim who writes that even if the egg is fully roasted it is still forbidden to insulate it, for the prohibition of insulating applies even to something fully cooked as written in siman 257. And one should also examine the Gra there.
169: (17) Introduction to the seif — there is no Torah prohibition of cooking except through heat from fire. The prohibition includes both cooking directly with fire, such as roasting or cooking on a stove, and cooking with something that was heated by fire (toldos ha'or). The Sages decreed that cooking with toldos chamah (derivatives of the sun) is also forbidden as a decree lest it be confused with toldos ha'or.
171: (18) 'With fire' — with heat from fire, and its prohibition is by Torah law.
173: (19) 'With toldos ha'or' — with something that was heated by fire, and this is also a Torah-level prohibition.
175: (20) 'So that it will roast' — these are examples of cooking on something that has been heated by fire, which is not cooking directly on the fire.
177: (21) 'With derivatives of the sun' — with something that was heated by the force of the sun, and it is also forbidden to cook with it.
179: (22) 'As a decree on account of toldos ha'or' — because a cloth heated by the sun resembles a cloth heated by fire, which is forbidden to cook with by Torah law, and therefore the Sages decreed against it.
181: (23) 'From the power of the sun' — and the prohibition is by rabbinic law.
183: (24) 'It is permitted' — because there is no concern that people will confuse heating directly in the sun with heating by fire.
185: The law of a solar water heater is like water boiled in the sun, which is permitted to use on Shabbos. And a solar heater combined with an electric heater is permitted only if the electricity was not activated on erev Shabbos.
